episode.subject: harbor seal
episode.title: The end without teeth
episode.body:
Something pinched my back. I turned. The bird had its head down, examining the sand.

I settled again. Another pinch.

This time I turned until my nose was where my tail had been. The bird walked around me.

I watched it go, and began turning again.

sourceEvidence: Independently read cached primary API observation100879811 in /tmp/freed-fenn145/gulls.json. Exact photo168417224 is cc-by, attributed Millie Basden. Observation identifies Phoca vitulina richardii and reports young Western Gull repeatedly trying to peck seal back. Subspecies supports species-level Fenn; no subspecies needs adding to canon.
imageReason: Sharp full seal body and face, recognizable juvenile gull behind its back. Neither actor is clipped. Sand serves as readable stage. Gull bill is open; no contact captured. Primary observed behavior supports the encounter beyond a generic juxtaposition.
proseReason: A repeated physical interruption changes Fenn from trying to rest into actively tracking the bird. The final turn keeps the predicament alive without a moral or injury gag. Strong sentences need no stylistic revision.
physicalPlausibility: Seal can turn its body on sand without sea-lion walking. Prose claims no hind-flipper rotation under the body, gallop or impossible reach. Nose replacing prior tail position describes a change of heading, not a human pivot technique. Turning speed is unspecified.
continuityReason: Full current two-entry arc reread. The ice scene is passive rotation of a resting group while Fenn declines involvement. This is active rotation of Fenn in response to a moving gull. Similar verb, different physical cause, desire and payoff. Childhood buoy play is distinct. Append as adult episode after both.
titleReason: The end without teeth names the gull preferred access and makes the seal repeated turning legible. Six words and first-person dispatch remains in body. Title does not falsely claim a bite.
fictionBoundary: Actual photograph shows proximity, not the pinch or turn sequence. Source observer reports attempted pecking; successful pinches, feigned sand examination and sequence are fiction. No recorded injury asserted. La Jolla remains source provenance, not travel from Kenai Fjords.
